title: Famous AI: The Best-Known Tools and What Sets Them Apart
summary: Which AI is the most famous, and why? Meet the best-known AI tools and milestones, and see how security and sales teams put them to work.
body_markdown:
The most famous AI in the world is ChatGPT, built by OpenAI. It became a household name in a way no earlier AI product had, and it is the reference point for nearly every other well-known AI tool today: Claude, Gemini, Midjourney, Copilot, Perplexity and more. Below we explain what makes each of them famous, which older milestones paved the way, and how fame differs from real business value, especially for security, risk, compliance and sales teams.

## TL;DR


- **ChatGPT is the most famous AI.**[Forbes calls GPT the name that towers above the rest](https://www.forbes.com/sites/bernardmarr/2024/07/24/what-is-the-most-famous-generative-ai/) in generative AI, and it launched the mainstream wave.
- **Fame comes in layers.** Historic milestones (Deep Blue, AlphaGo), consumer assistants (Alexa, Siri) and generative tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Gemini, Claude) are famous for different reasons.
- **Famous is not the same as useful for your workflow.** The advantage is shifting from the model itself to how well a business plugs AI into measurable, specialized work.
- **Security and sales teams get the most from structured, repetitive tasks** , such as answering security questionnaires, where purpose-built tools and your own approved content matter more than a famous brand name.

## What is the most famous AI?


If you ask a hundred people to name an AI, most will say ChatGPT. According to[a 2026 overview of famous AI](https://beginnersinai.org/famous-ai/) , ChatGPT launched on November 30, 2022 and reached 100 million users in two months.[Forbes contributor Bernard Marr](https://www.forbes.com/sites/bernardmarr/2024/07/24/what-is-the-most-famous-generative-ai/) explains the fame this way: it was the first AI to show advanced generative abilities to the general public, and it became the fastest-growing consumer application in history.


Three things explain why it stuck:


1. **Zero friction.** You type in plain language and get an answer. No installation, no training.[OpenAI states that ChatGPT is free to use](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6783457-what-is-chatgpt) , with subscription plans available for more capability.
2. **Versatility.** The same chat box drafts emails, explains code, summarizes documents and brainstorms.
3. **Timing.** It arrived when search and productivity giants were ready to compete on AI, so every announcement afterward was measured against it.


EY's Jeffrey Wong put the shift in business terms in[a CNBC explainer](https://www.cnbc.com/2023/02/08/what-is-chatgpt-viral-ai-chatbot-at-heart-of-microsoft-google-fight.html) : the breakthrough is that these tools perform human-like tasks in ways once thought impossible for computers. That is why companies started asking not "what is it?" but "where do we use it?"


### A note on the name


"GPT" stands for generative pre-trained transformer, a type of large language model built on the transformer architecture.[Wikipedia's overview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_pre-trained_transformer) notes that OpenAI was the first to apply generative pre-training to that architecture, in 2018, and that OpenAI has asserted GPT as its brand. So "GPT" is both a technical term and a company name, which is one reason it appears everywhere.


## The most famous AI tools you will hear about


ChatGPT is the headliner, but it is not alone.[Built In's list of top AI tools](https://builtin.com/artificial-intelligence/ai-tools) includes ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini, Midjourney, ElevenLabs, Copilot, Meta AI and GitHub. Here is how the best-known names differ in practice.

ChatGPT OpenAI General conversational AI for writing, analysis and code

The capability descriptions for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Midjourney and DALL-E follow[this 2026 guide to famous AI](https://beginnersinai.org/famous-ai/) . Pricing moves quickly, so treat the following as 2026 snapshots.[Amazon lists Alexa+](https://www.amazon.com/alexaplus/dp/B0CXRRF584) as free with Prime or $19.99 per month on the Standard plan in the United States, and the same guide to famous AI puts Gemini Advanced at $19.99 per month. Always check the provider's own page before you budget.


### Why "famous" and "best" are different questions


People also ask what the best AI is and whether ChatGPT is still on top. There is no single answer, because the best tool depends on the job. A designer wants an image model, a developer wants a coding assistant, and a security analyst wants accurate answers grounded in company policy. Popularity tells you which tool most people have heard of. It does not tell you which one fits your task, your data rules or your accuracy bar.


## Famous AI before ChatGPT


ChatGPT did not invent public fascination with AI. Two moments earlier set the stage, as summarized in[a timeline of AI milestones](https://mediaandthemachine.substack.com/p/the-top-20-milestones-in-ai-1943) :


- **Deep Blue (1997).** On May 11, 1997, IBM's Deep Blue beat world chess champion Garry Kasparov, the first time a computer defeated a reigning champion in a match under tournament conditions. It showed machines could outperform people at complex, rule-bound decisions.
- **AlphaGo (2016).** On March 15, 2016, DeepMind's AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol, one of the world's best Go players, in a game long considered too intuitive for computers.


The pattern is useful. Each milestone solved a narrow problem extremely well. Generative AI is different in breadth: one model handles many kinds of language tasks. That breadth is what pulled AI out of research labs and into everyday work.


### Famous AI in fiction


Much of what readers mean by "famous AI" is cultural: HAL 9000, the replicants of *Blade Runner* , GERTY in *Moon* . These characters shaped expectations, and fears, long before real chatbots existed. If that angle interests you, we wrote about[fictional artificial intelligence, its origins, tropes and real lessons](https://blog.skypher.co/blog/fictional-artificial-intelligence) .


## How the economics of famous AI shape what you can buy


Fame has a financial side. Heavy investment explains why AI features appear in so many products at once. For a closer look at the numbers behind the best-known AI company, see[OpenAI revenue and statistics](https://babylovegrowth.ai/blog/open-ai-revenue-stats) . The practical takeaway for a buyer is that the market is crowded and moving fast, so a vendor's name recognition is a weak signal compared with fit, controls and results.


## How businesses actually use famous AI


In business, the famous tools show up in three ways.


**As general assistants.** Teams use chat tools to draft, summarize and brainstorm. OpenAI describes[ChatGPT Enterprise](https://chatgpt.com/zh-Hant/business/enterprise/) as connecting approved tools, files and team workflows, with access, security and compliance controls for business use.


**As embedded features.** Gemini inside Workspace, Copilot inside developer tools and similar integrations put AI where people already work.


**As the engine under specialized software.** This is where gains tend to be easiest to measure. According to[Entrepreneur's coverage of the Stanford report](https://spanish.entrepreneur.com/tecnologia/usar-ia-ya-no-te-distingue-lo-que-el-nuevo-informe-de-stanford-revela) , value is most measurable in repetitive, structured tasks: customer service agents resolving 14 to 15 percent more cases per hour, and marketers increasing production by 50 percent. The same analysis argues that the competitive edge is moving from the models themselves to how well companies integrate them into specialized, measurable workflows.


That last point matters for anyone in security, risk or sales. Your most repetitive, structured work probably is not writing poems with a chatbot. It is answering the same questions about encryption, access control, incident response and data retention, over and over, for every prospect and every vendor review.


## Using famous AI safely at work


Well-known tools are powerful and uneven. Stanford researchers describe a "jagged frontier": models can win math olympiads yet fail at basic tasks such as reading an analog clock, as[Entrepreneur reports](https://spanish.entrepreneur.com/tecnologia/usar-ia-ya-no-te-distingue-lo-que-el-nuevo-informe-de-stanford-revela) . For a security or compliance team, that unevenness is the whole risk: an answer can sound fluent and still be wrong in one detail that a customer will notice.


A July 2025 incident with Gemini CLI shows what happens when an AI agent acts on a wrong internal assumption without safeguards:[project files were permanently deleted](https://www.oneindia.com/in-the-news/new-rules-building-ai-products-responsible-development-stanford-index-012-8180637.html) because there was no rollback protection. In the same coverage, Sumeet Ram argues that fast adoption calls for more discipline, with guardrails coming first.


A short checklist we recommend before you let any AI touch customer-facing or compliance content:


1. **Ground answers in approved sources.** Use your own policies, past answers and certifications as the single source of truth.
2. **Keep a human reviewer in the loop** for anything a customer or auditor will rely on.
3. **Look for a confidence signal** so reviewers know which answers need attention first.
4. **Protect rollback.** Version your content so a bad change can be reversed.
5. **Control access.** Decide who can edit the knowledge base and who can only read it.

We talk with security, GRC and sales teams every week, and the pattern is consistent. They have all tried the famous chat tools. They are impressed, and then they hit the same wall: a general assistant does not know your latest SOC 2 scope, your encryption standards or the wording you approved last quarter.


That is why we built Skypher around a different idea. Instead of asking one famous model to improvise, we designed our platform with proprietary retrieval AI that answers from your own knowledge base, attaches a confidence score to each answer, and works with the formats questionnaires actually arrive in. Our view, in short:


- **The model is a commodity; the context is yours.** What differentiates results is the quality and structure of your approved content.
- **Integration beats novelty.** Connecting to the portals and tools your teams already use (we support over 40 third-party risk management platforms and enterprise tools, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Confluence, Notion, Google Drive, OneDrive and SharePoint) removes the copy-and-paste step where errors creep in.

ChatGPT is the most famous AI because it made generative AI usable by anyone, overnight. Claude, Gemini, Midjourney, Alexa and others each carved out a reputation in a specific area, and Deep Blue and AlphaGo showed the way decades earlier. ## FAQ


### What is the most famous AI?


ChatGPT from OpenAI is widely seen as the most famous AI. It launched on November 30, 2022 and reached 100 million users within two months, according to a[2026 guide to famous AI](https://beginnersinai.org/famous-ai/) . Its fame comes from being free to try, easy to use and useful for many tasks.


### What are the big names in AI today?


The tools most often named are ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Midjourney, Copilot and Meta AI, as listed by[Built In](https://builtin.com/artificial-intelligence/ai-tools) . Behind them stand companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Each is known for a different strength, from conversation to images to workplace integration.


### Is ChatGPT still the best AI?


It is still the best known, but "best" depends on the task. Some tools are better at long documents, image creation or tight integration with a particular workspace. Test the candidates on your own real work, such as a sample questionnaire, and judge on accuracy and review time.


### Are famous AI tools safe to use for security questionnaires?


General chat tools can help with drafting, but answers about your controls must come from approved, current content and be reviewed by a person. Stanford researchers describe[AI abilities as uneven](https://spanish.entrepreneur.com/tecnologia/usar-ia-ya-no-te-distingue-lo-que-el-nuevo-informe-de-stanford-revela) , so a review step and a confidence signal are good practice. Purpose-built tools like ours are designed around that workflow.


### What was the first famous AI?


For the public, an early landmark was IBM's Deep Blue, which beat Garry Kasparov on May 11, 1997, as noted in[this AI milestones timeline](https://mediaandthemachine.substack.com/p/the-top-20-milestones-in-ai-1943) . AlphaGo's 2016 win over Lee Sedol was the next major moment. ChatGPT in 2022 brought AI to everyday users.
